title: Where the individual data sit decides the error of a population-adjusted network contrast at the same total sample size
question: At a fixed total sample size, does the error of a population-adjusted network contrast depend on the network's topology and on which trial supplies individual data, beyond total information?
design: Exact calculation: four-treatment line, star, loop-with-tail and two-path networks with 1200 patients in total, one individual-data trial standardized to the target on each edge in turn, effect modification of three strengths and two target shifts.
answer: No. At 1200 patients in every network, the probability of getting the sign of the decision contrast wrong ranged from 0.36 to 0.93 across four topologies and positions of the one individual-data trial (moderate modification, target shifted one SD), and the spread exceeded 0.10 in every scenario. An individual-data trial off every path to the contrast carried zero weight and changed nothing; standardizing one edge could raise the bias (0.20 to 0.30 in a line network) by removing an error that had offset the others.
findings: Star network: IPD on A-B or A-C has zero weight on D versus A; only the direct A-D trial removes the bias.
Line network: standardizing B-C gave an unbiased estimate by cancellation of the remaining edges' modification differences.
Coverage ranged from 0.02 to 0.95 across configurations at the strongest modification.
not_answered: Deterministic calculation; continuous outcome, linear modification, four hand-built topologies, one IPD trial, fixed-effect model; no generated topology families, component networks or ML-NMR. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: D versus A mean difference in the target population
methods_compared: network meta-analysis with one trial standardized to the target, placed on each edge in turn, across four topologies
n_sim: Exact calculation: 4 topologies x all placements x 3 modification strengths x 2 target shifts
